categories.label: Dimensional / Geometric
categories.desc: Dimension discrepancies between sheets, conflicting datums, wall assembly totals that don't match their component layers, and missing code-critical dimensions.

categories.label: Building Envelope
categories.desc: Vapor control, air barrier continuity, insulation placement and values, flashing details, and whether wall and roof assemblies perform appropriately for the project climate.

categories.label: Code and Life Safety
categories.desc: Egress paths, minimum door and railing dimensions, fire separation requirements, makeup air for exhaust systems, and other conditions requiring code compliance.

categories.label: Constructability
categories.desc: Whether details can physically be built as drawn — door swing clearances, missing flashing, system conflicts, and architectural elements that require coordination not shown.

categories.label: Schedule-to-Drawing
categories.desc: Door and window schedule entries that conflict with what is drawn on plans or elevations — wrong widths, wrong materials, wrong finishes for the assigned room.

categories.label: Spec-to-Drawing Conflicts
categories.desc: Conflicts between the project specifications and the drawn documents — different products, different quantities, different performance requirements, different assembly configurations.

categories.label: Completeness and Clarity
categories.desc: Missing tags, orphaned keynotes, TBD items that prevent accurate bidding, dead cross-references, deferred design decisions, and annotations that are ambiguous or absent.

runs.notes: Run 1 of 3. 98 findings. Strongest code-side coverage of the three on A/E but the only run besides run 3 to take penalties. Full catches on both halves of A1 (door 11-1 unscheduled and door 10-1 unplanned), D4 (double vapor barrier on E-1, which run 2 missed), and G3 (orphaned keynote 13). Missed the whole roof-tag drafting cluster - neither G1 (blank tag) nor G14 (R-2 undefined) appears anywhere in this run, which never mentions R-2 at all. Two penalties, both judgment calls worth a spot-check: the HERO-code claim is I2 stated flatly at High confidence, and B-2 is an unseeded enlarged-plan dimension-chain claim at High confidence, which is the substance of the corresponding Known Incorrect Findings entry. Notably it avoided two traps: it read the stair as 18 risers (N33, not the I8 misread) and it described the south pool edge as relying on the pool wall rather than claiming the enclosure is non-compliant, so neither is penalized.

Run 2 of 3 and the best of the three. 111 findings, no penalties. Clean sweep of category E (8/8) - the only run to take E6 in full, naming the 650 CFM hood against the spec's unresolved make-up air question. Also the only run to catch B5 (states outright that stair width and headroom are not dimensioned on A3.22) and D6 (near-verbatim: no drawing identifies the air-barrier layer or its continuity at wall-to-roof and wall-to-foundation transitions). Correctly separates G14 (R-2 called out on A3.01, undefined on A4.01) while still missing G1, since it never observes the blank tag. G16 scores 0.5 rather than 1.0: it names the right walls and correctly says they are tagged W-2/W-4 or untagged, but prefixes that with the false claim that no acoustic wall type exists on A4.00 - W-3 is defined there. That false half is not the specific claim the G16 row penalizes (W-3 untagged on any floor plan), so it is scored as a partial rather than an incorrect finding; worth a spot-check. The 3-point gap to run 1 is almost entirely confidence calibration: this run hedged the HERO-code claim to Moderate with 'possibly HERS' and hedged the enlarged-plan chain to Moderate while noting the reference points are not indicated, so neither is penalized under the hedging rule.

Run 3 of 3 and the weakest. 116 findings - the most of the three, and the least accurate. Only run to miss E1 outright: the 1'-10" Powder Room door width appears nowhere, despite runs 1 and 2 both flagging it. Also lost D5, D6 and G3, which the other runs caught. Strongest C-series reading of the three - C6 is the cleanest statement of the single-spec-slope vs three-drawn-slopes conflict, and it adds the 1/8":12 entry canopies. E5 scores 0.5: it flags the pool barrier cable infill as climbable but never reaches the 4" maximum opening / cable spacing that the row is about. E-2 hedges 'possibly 13-1 into the Office' - 13-1 is office-to-hallway, not a garage door - but the catch rests on the correctly named North Hallway door, so E8 still scores. One penalty: unlike run 1, this run asserts flatly that no guard is provided at the open south pool edge, at High confidence, which is the known-incorrect south-pool-edge reading. Flagged for spot-check, since the model frames it as fall protection rather than pool-barrier enclosure. F-3 (PT furring in direct contact with Galvalume panels, a corrosion incompatibility) is specific, confident and matches nothing on any list - a candidate for the neutral list.

Its HERO-code claim matches I2 but is hedged at Moderate, so it is not penalized.
